checkpoints.description: [1/2] Desktop workbench: first-class editor, browser and terminal in the right pane; unified lower-left Workspace section.

impact_assessment.why: The right pane and lower-left rail were cramped and lacked dedicated editor/browser/terminal surfaces; desktop is the target (G-011).
impact_assessment.benefits: Clearer tool access, side-by-side editor, browser navigation, terminal tab.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tab order and Alt shortcuts; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Preserve testids and Alt mapping, keep original tab labels for screenshot inventory, verify with UI shots and tests.

checkpoints.description: Desktop workbench implemented: Files pane is a side-by-side Explorer+editor; Preview pane is a Browser with Back/Forward/Reload/Detect; terminal is a first-class tab; lower-left is one Workspace section. G-007/G-010 vision review of before/after shots at desktop/narrow/tablet, dark and light: no clipping, overlap, contrast or stale copy; desktop target per G-011. npm test: 125 files / 678 tests passed.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Make the shell genuinely desktop-only: remove overlay states, mobile controls and responsive breakpoints; target gates/screenshots at 1440px.

impact_assessment.why: The user declared the product desktop-only; leftover mobile chrome and narrow/tablet gates kept the layout split.
impact_assessment.benefits: One three-pane desktop shell; no dead controls; verification matches the supported viewport.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tab/testids preserved; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep workspace-reopen for collapsed workspace, update guidelines+ADR-124, verify with browser gate and screenshots.
